original_question: Can one construct strong invariants for welded knots and welded braids, classify welded knots if possible, and determine whether Satoh's mapping from welded knots or links to ambient isotopy classes of ribbon torus embeddings in four-dimensional space is faithful?
target_in_paper: Section 7, Problem 6 (Welded knots): the paper asks for good invariants and, if possible, a classification of welded knots, and then asks whether Satoh's map from welded knots (links) to ambient isotopy classes of ribbon torus embeddings in four-space is faithful. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/89015))
correct_elements: Your draft captures the core of Problem 6: it asks about invariants for welded knots, possible classification of welded knots, and the faithfulness of Satoh's map to ribbon torus embeddings in four-dimensional space. It also notices the nearby braid context, since the paper states that every welded knot is the closure of a welded braid. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/89015))
missing_details: The paper says good invariants, not strong invariants. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/89015))

Welded knots are the equivalence classes obtained from virtual link diagrams by allowing only one forbidden move, for example the upper forbidden move. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/89015))

The nearby motivation is that the fundamental group and the quandle of a virtual diagram are invariant under the upper forbidden move. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/89015))

Welded braids are mentioned only as context: they were studied earlier, and every welded knot is the closure of a welded braid; Problem 6 itself does not separately ask for a classification of welded braids. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/89015))

The faithfulness question is asked for equivalence classes of welded knots (links), not merely for individual diagrams. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/89015))

The codomain must be stated exactly as ambient isotopy classes of embeddings of tori, ribbon tori to be exact, in four-dimensional space/four-space. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/89015))

The paper records an important partial result: Satoh's map already induces an isomorphism from the welded knot's combinatorial fundamental group, in fact its quandle, to the fundamental group of the complement of the associated torus embedding. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/89015))
refined_question: Let a welded knot be the equivalence class of a virtual knot diagram under the generalized Reidemeister moves together with only one forbidden move (for example, the upper forbidden move). Since the fundamental group and quandle are invariant under this upper forbidden move and every welded knot is the closure of a welded braid, can one construct good invariants of welded knots and, if possible, classify welded knots; and, for welded knots or links, is Satoh's map from these equivalence classes to ambient isotopy classes of ribbon torus embeddings in four-space faithful, even though it is already known to induce an isomorphism from the welded knot's combinatorial fundamental group, indeed quandle, to the fundamental group of the complement of the corresponding torus embedding? ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/89015))
justification: This is the nearest paper-faithful formulation because your draft matches Section 7, Problem 6 rather than the separate Problem 9 on virtual braids: Problem 6 explicitly frames welded knots via the one-forbidden-move quotient, mentions welded braids only to say that every welded knot is a braid closure, asks for good invariants and possible classification of welded knots, and ends with the faithfulness question for Satoh's ribbon-torus map. The earlier discussion that virtual-knot groups can be interpreted as complement groups of tori embedded in four-dimensional Euclidean space supplies the surrounding geometric context. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/89015))
